![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/90d5e9115d216f2a7f8fba49295a36b95cd932c4df7f8bace1b45e3542e9ae11.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/ec2f6c67eee7f836cc71efec2b17c2276aa8a9d397c632b3c499a46a75f7b95c.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={({\rho }^{2})}^{3} \\  & ={\rho }^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}^{3}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{6}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}{\rho }^{8}\,d\rho  \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{9}{\rho }^{9}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =1} \\  & =-(0-1)\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\cdot \frac{1}{9}(1-0) \\  & =1\cdot \pi \cdot \frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{9}\end{aligned}
$$
